name: Ashwatthama
role: Son of Drona, warrior and chiranjivi of the Mahabharata
summary: Ashwatthama is the son of Drona and a top-ranked warrior of the Kaurava side in the Mahabharata. The epic says he was born with a gem on his forehead, and tradition counts him among the seven chiranjivi, beings who live on.
about: In the Mahabharata, Ashwatthama is the son of the teacher Drona and Kripi, and he trained with the Kuru princes. The epic says he was born with a gem on his forehead and that his first cry sounded like a neighing horse, which gave him his name. He was a Maharathi, skilled with divine weapons including the Narayanastra and Brahmashirastra. After Drona's fall and Duryodhana's defeat, he made a night raid on the sleeping Pandava camp, and then loosed a Brahmashirastra at the Pandava line. The sages Vyasa and Narada stepped between the two weapons: Arjuna drew his back, but Ashwatthama could not. The gem was taken from him, and Krishna, who restored the unborn Parikshit, cursed him to wander for 3,000 years. Hindus count him among the chiranjivi, and local traditions place him at temples such as Gupteshwar Mahadev in Asirgarh Fort in Madhya Pradesh. Modern retellings, including the 2024 film Kalki 2898 AD, show him still wandering.
kidSummary: Ashwatthama is Drona's son in the Mahabharata. The epic says he was born with a shining gem on his forehead, and his first cry sounded like a horse. He is one of the seven chiranjivi, people tradition says live for a very long time. Many stories say he still walks the earth.

story.title: A horse-like cry
story.text: In the Mahabharata, Drona's son cried like a neighing horse when he was born. A voice from above then named him Ashwatthama, and he had a gem on his forehead.

story.title: Flour water
story.text: Drona was so poor that his young son once received flour mixed with water instead of milk. Drona later taught him all he knew, including secret weapons.

story.title: The false news
story.text: On day fifteen, Bhima killed an elephant named Ashwatthama. Drona heard a half-truth that his son was dead and laid down his weapons.

story.title: The night raid
story.text: After the main battle, an owl attacking sleeping crows gave him an idea. He prayed to Shiva and attacked the sleeping Pandava camp, and the epic treats this as a deeply sorrowful act.

story.title: The long wandering
story.text: The epic says Ashwatthama aimed a mighty weapon at the unborn Parikshit, but Krishna restored the child. Krishna cursed him to wander in pain for 3,000 years, and his gem was taken.

teaches: Anger can lead people to regret
Being a good son does not excuse a harmful act
The need to think before using power

facts.text: Ashwatthama's name is traced to words for horse and strength. The epic says his birth cry sounded like a celestial horse neighing, and a divine voice then named him.
In the Mahabharata he was born with a gem on his forehead that gave him special powers.
Epic tradition describes him as made of parts of Shiva, Yama, Kama and Krodha. During the war, the sage Vyasa told him he was a partial incarnation of Shiva.
As a child he was given rice-flour water in place of milk and was found weeping over it, a scene often retold about Drona's poverty.

In some versions of the epic, Drona gave his son extra archery lessons while the other pupils were away fetching water. Arjuna noticed, and he hurried through his own chores so he could join those lessons.
When Ashwatthama and Arjuna each loosed a Brahmashirsha weapon, the sages Vyasa and Narada stepped between them. Arjuna managed to pull his weapon back, but Ashwatthama did not know how.
After Karna fell, Ashwatthama tried to talk Duryodhana into making peace, but his advice was ignored.
Later in the fighting he used the Agneya weapon against Arjuna, and Arjuna answered with a Brahma weapon that cancelled it.
His Narayanastra could be used only once. Krishna told the Pandavas to put down their weapons to stop it; Bhima refused, until Arjuna shielded him with a Varuna weapon.

After the night raid, Draupadi vowed to fast until death unless Ashwatthama was brought to justice. Bhima set out after him with Nakula as his charioteer, and Krishna warned the other Pandavas to follow.
Fleeing after the raid, he took shelter at Vyasa's hermitage, and the Pandavas found him there dressed as an ascetic.
The idea for the night raid came when an owl attacked sleeping crows. The epic places this under a huge banyan tree, where he and the two other Kaurava survivors had taken shelter.
The Sapta Chiranjivi Stotram, a well-known Sanskrit prayer, names Ashwatthama among the long-lived ones. Tradition says that remembering these names brings freedom from illness and a long life.
The Razmnama, the Mughal-era Persian translation of the Mahabharata, has painted folios showing Ashwatthama's duel with Dhrishtadyumna (about 1598) and his launch of the Narayanastra.
He charged a blade of grass with the Brahmashirastra to target the Pandava line. It struck Uttara's womb, and Krishna protected the unborn Parikshit.
The epic says Vyasa offered to spare his life if he gave up the gem on his forehead, and Krishna cursed him to wander for 3,000 years.
A shrine to him is located inside the Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram.
Local tradition says he visits the Gupteshwar Mahadev Temple inside Asirgarh Fort each morning to worship Shiva with flowers.
At the gate of the Pandava camp, a terrifying shape blocked his way and he could not defeat it. Only after he offered himself to Shiva did the god enter him and grant a celestial sword.
Some historians, including D. C. Sircar and R. Sathianathaier, note that the Pallava kings of Kanchi told a family legend of an ancestor descended from Ashwatthama and a Naga princess.

In the 2024 film Kalki 2898 AD, directed by Nag Ashwin, Amitabh Bachchan plays Ashwatthama, who has wandered for nearly six thousand years. That is longer than the 3,000 years the epic gives, because the film is set in 2898 AD.
Folk stories say the wound left where the gem was removed never closes, so Ashwatthama wanders in pain. Tales tell of sightings of a tall man with an unhealed scar on his forehead.

quiz.q: What sound did baby Ashwatthama make, giving him his name?
quiz.why: His cry sounded like a horse neighing.

quiz.q: What was on his forehead from birth, in the epic?
quiz.why: The gem gave him special powers.

quiz.q: How long was his wandering curse in the Mahabharata?
quiz.why: Krishna cursed him to wander for 3,000 years.

quiz.q: Which fort in Madhya Pradesh is linked to him by local tradition?
quiz.why: He is said to worship Shiva there each morning.

quiz.q: Who plays Ashwatthama in the film Kalki 2898 AD?
quiz.why: Amitabh Bachchan took the role in 2024.
